steps.title: Three levels
steps.body: Beaujolais has three main levels. Beaujolais, mostly from the south, light and fruity. Beaujolais-Villages, from 38 villages in the north, with more depth. And the ten crus, named villages on granite, at the top. Crus labels often don't say Beaujolais at all, just the village name.

steps.title: Light to structured
steps.body: The ten crus, north to south: Saint-Amour, Juliénas, Chénas, Moulin-à-Vent, Fleurie, Chiroubles, Morgon, Régnié, Brouilly and Côte de Brouilly. Fleurie, Chiroubles and Saint-Amour are light and floral. Morgon, on decomposed schist, and Moulin-à-Vent, on granite with manganese, are the most structured and age well.
steps.highlight: Fleurie floral; Morgon and Moulin-à-Vent firm

steps.prompt: Match each cru to its style.
steps.explanation: The crus range from light to structured.

steps.body: Aged Morgon and Moulin-à-Vent can taste like Burgundy. Locals say the wine pinote, becomes Pinot-like, with age.

steps.explanation: Ten named villages on the northern granite.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Beaujolais has three levels: Beaujolais, Villages, crus
The ten crus range from light Fleurie to firm Moulin-à-Vent
Morgon and Moulin-à-Vent can age like Burgundy
